Such are the fruits of impatience, of the incapacity to bear
our burdens and to wait, to lend a hand patiently so that in
time the evil may diminish. Impatience leads only to a
worsening of our troubles. It poisons the atmosphere. And
what we need above all is an atmosphere that is antiseptic,
an atmosphere of mutual confidence, mutual helpfulness,
composure, cheerfulness and humour. How cleansing and
salutary it is if in the press and turmoil where each one has to
bear his share of inconvenience, there is to be found some-
one who manages to preserve his composure, and with a
touch of dry humour can make a witty remark. Now, such an
atmosphere of trust and helpfulness and humour springs
from the spirit of patience.
Again, impatience is mischievous in regard to our relations
with our conquerors. There is no doubt about it that their
hand lies heavy upon us. But it will only become lighter
when we win their confidence. In fact in proportion as we
have gained it, we have noticed their readiness to meet us
halfway and their good will in endeavouring to ease our lot.
By impatience we can only aggravate our evil situation in the
world. How cheap are the wild accusations which fly to and
fro! How cheap and how foolish! Were we patient we should
not always be thinking of what must ever seem so unpleasant
and deplorable when foreign troops have occupied our soil.
Nor should we be only thinking of the worse things that have
been spared us (for things might have been much worse)
but we should consider above all the positive help that has
been given us, and that readiness to meet us which has been
manifested. again and again. The spirit of patience affords
us calm of mind for reflection and so the ability to cleave to
the good rather than become obsessed by the evil. Impatience
forgets the misery that we ourselves have brought upon the
world and the suffering we have caused to so many peoples.
Will they so easily forget these miseries? We need patience
in order to regain their confidence.
